title: Arjuna asks to see the cosmic form

verses.sa: अर्जुन उवाचमदनुग्रहाय परमं गुह्यमध्यात्मसंज्ञितम् । यत्त्वयोक्तं वचस्तेन मोहोऽयं विगतो मम ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna says: By the gracious words you spoke for my benefit alone, my delusion has been dispelled.
verses.angle: A secret teaching for one person
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna is not asking a new question now, but answering the one Krishna just asked. Listen for the one thing he says has already cleared his mind.

body.text: Arjuna says: By the gracious words you spoke for my benefit alone, my delusion has been dispelled. Arjuna says his delusion is gone because of the words Krishna spoke. The secret teaching was given for Arjuna alone, and with that, the confusion is simply gone. He asks to see the cosmic form of the Lord, having heard about the birth and death of all beings.

verses.sa: भवाप्ययौ हि भूतानां श्रुतौ विस्तरशो मया । त्वत्तः कमलपत्राक्ष माहात्म्यमपि चाव्ययम् ॥
verses.tr: O lotus-eyed one, I have heard from You in detail about the arising and passing away of all beings, and also about Your imperishable majesty.
verses.angle: Kamalapatraksha: lotus-eyed, pointing to the eyes
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna stops arguing and tells Krishna what he has learned. Listen to the one name he uses for him.

body.text: O lotus-eyed one, I have heard from You in detail about the arising and passing away of all beings, and also about Your imperishable majesty. Arjuna calls him Kamalapatraksha, lotus-eyed. This name points to the eyes. Arjuna has heard about the imperishable majesty, and is ready to see it. He asks to see the divine form, saying everything Krishna has said is true.

verses.sa: एवमेतद्यथात्थ त्वमात्मानं परमेश्वर । द्रष्टुमिच्छामि ते रूपमैश्वरं पुरुषोत्तम ॥
verses.tr: O Supreme Person, everything you have said about yourself is true. Yet I wish to see your divine form.
verses.angle: Arjuna asks for sight beyond words
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna has heard Krishna's words, and now he asks for something beyond hearing. Listen for the shift from belief to sight.

body.text: O Supreme Person, everything you have said about yourself is true. Yet I wish to see your divine form. Arjuna believes every word Krishna said about himself, and still asks to see the divine form with his eyes. Arjuna asks Krishna to show that imperishable self if he thinks Arjuna can bear to see it.

verses.sa: मन्यसे यदि तच्छक्यं मया द्रष्टुमिति प्रभो । योगेश्वर ततो मे त्वं दर्शयाऽत्मानमव्ययम् ॥
verses.tr: If you think I can see that form, Lord, then show me your imperishable self, Master of yoga.
verses.angle: Arjuna leaves the choice to Krishna
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna has asked to see the divine form, but now he faces a doubt. Listen to how he hands the choice over to the Master of yoga.

body.text: If you think I can see that form, Lord, then show me your imperishable self, Master of yoga. Arjuna does not demand the vision; he says, if you think I can see it, then show me. He leaves the power to grant the vision entirely to Krishna, the master of yoga. Krishna answers by opening his vision to thousands of forms, divine and many-colored, visible to Arjuna alone.

verses.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचपश्य मे पार्थ रूपाणि शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः । नानाविधानि दिव्यानि नानावर्णाकृतीनि च ॥
verses.tr: The Blessed Lord says: See, Partha, my forms in hundreds and thousands, diverse, divine, and of many colors and shapes.
verses.angle: Partha, son of Pritha, meaning here
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna stands ready to reveal more than Arjuna ever asked for. Listen to what he asks him to look at.

body.text: The Blessed Lord says: See, Partha, my forms in hundreds and thousands, diverse, divine, and of many colors and shapes. Krishna addresses him as Partha, son of Pritha, and tells him to see hundreds of thousands of divine forms. The word rupani, forms, shows this is not one body but a universe of shapes and colors. He then lists the Adityas, Vasus, and Rudras, showing Arjuna the gods themselves gathered in one vision.

verses.tr: See the twelve Adityas, the eight Vasus, the eleven Rudras, the two Ashvins, and the forty-nine Maruts. See many wonders never seen before, O Bharata.
verses.angle: Adityas, Vasus, Rudras, Ashvins, and Maruts inside Krishna
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Listen for the names of the deities Krishna points to inside his own form. Notice the exact list he gives.

body.text: See the twelve Adityas, the eight Vasus, the eleven Rudras, the two Ashvins, and the forty-nine Maruts. See many wonders never seen before, O Bharata. Adityas, Vasus, Rudras, Ashvins and Maruts appear inside Krishna, wonders Arjuna has never seen before. Krishna now tells Arjuna to look at the whole universe gathered in one place in his body.

verses.sa: इहैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं पश्याद्य सचराचरम् । मम देहे गुडाकेश यच्चान्यद्द्रष्टुमिच्छसि ॥
verses.tr: Behold the entire universe, with all that moves and does not move, gathered here in one place in My body. See whatever else you wish to see as well.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just shown Arjuna the twelve Adityas, Vasus, Rudras, and Maruts. Now He tells Arjuna to look closer at His body.

body.text: Behold the entire universe, with all that moves and does not move, gathered here in one place in My body. See whatever else you wish to see as well. Krishna addresses Arjuna as Gudakesha, the conqueror of sleep. He commands him to see the entire moving and unmoving world placed in one spot inside His body, as if the universe were a single object. Krishna tells Arjuna he cannot see this with ordinary eyes and must be given divine sight instead.

verses.sa: न तु मां शक्यसे द्रष्टुमनेनैव स्वचक्षुषा । दिव्यं ददामि ते चक्षुः पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम् ॥
verses.tr: You cannot see me with these ordinary eyes. I give you divine sight, so you may behold my supreme power.
verses.angle: Ordinary eyes cannot see the divine form
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Arjuna asked to see the cosmic form, and Krishna showed him the universe gathered in his body. But ordinary sight is not enough.

body.text: You cannot see me with these ordinary eyes. I give you divine sight, so you may behold my supreme power. Krishna tells Arjuna that he cannot see him with these only, own eyes, and because of that, he gives him divine sight to see his supreme power. Sanjaya now tells Dhritarashtra that Krishna revealed the supreme divine form to Arjuna.

verses.sa: सञ्जय उवाचएवमुक्त्वा ततो राजन्महायोगेश्वरो हरिः । दर्शयामास पार्थाय परमं रूपमैश्वरम् ॥
verses.tr: Sanjaya says: Having spoken thus, O King, the great lord of yoga, Hari, revealed to Arjuna the supreme divine form.
verses.angle: Divine sight and the supreme form
verses.speaker: Sanjaya

intro.text: After Krishna grants Arjuna divine sight to see beyond the physical, what does Arjuna witness? Listen to Sanjaya's account of the revelation.

body.text: Sanjaya says: Having spoken thus, O King, the great lord of yoga, Hari, revealed to Arjuna the supreme divine form. Sanjaya tells Dhritarashtra that the great lord of yoga, Hari, reveals to Partha the supreme divine form, the very cosmic reality Arjuna asked to see. Sanjaya then describes the many mouths, eyes, and divine weapons on this form.

verses.tr: With many mouths and eyes, with countless wondrous forms, adorned with many divine ornaments and many uplifted divine weapons.
verses.speaker: Sanjaya

intro.text: Arjuna has just received divine sight. Listen to how Sanjaya begins to describe what he sees.

body.text: With many mouths and eyes, with countless wondrous forms, adorned with many divine ornaments and many uplifted divine weapons. Sanjaya begins a list, repeating the word many, or anek. The form is not a single body but a vast scene filled with countless faces, eyes, ornaments, and raised weapons. The vision continues with the form facing everywhere, wearing garlands and divine garments.

verses.tr: Wearing divine garlands and garments, anointed with divine fragrances, wondrous in every way, endless, and facing everywhere.
verses.angle: Divya: the word that marks the otherworldly
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Listen for one word that repeats like a drumbeat in this verse, marking everything you see as coming from a source beyond this world.

body.text: Wearing divine garlands and garments, anointed with divine fragrances, wondrous in every way, endless, and facing everywhere. The word is divya. It means divine, and it appears again and again: divine garlands, divine clothes, divine fragrance, divine ornaments, divine weapons. The vision is not merely grand; it is repeatedly set apart as otherworldly. Arjuna feels that even a thousand suns could not equal the light of this being.

verses.sa: दिवि सूर्यसहस्रस्य भवेद्युगपदुत्थिता । यदि भाः सदृशी सा स्याद्भासस्तस्य महात्मनः ॥
verses.tr: If a thousand suns rose together in the sky, their light would still barely match that great being's radiance.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna stares at the form that has swallowed the battlefield, and tries to name its light. Listen to how he measures the form against the sky itself.

body.text: If a thousand suns rose together in the sky, their light would still barely match that great being's radiance. Arjuna is not describing a man, but a radiance that dwarfs the sky. He says that even a thousand suns rising at once would barely equal the light of that one great being. He now looks inside that body and sees the whole universe gathered in one place.

verses.sa: तत्रैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं प्रविभक्तमनेकधा । अपश्यद्देवदेवस्य शरीरे पाण्डवस्तदा ॥
verses.tr: There Arjuna saw the entire universe gathered in one place, divided in countless ways within the body of the Lord of the gods.
verses.angle: ekastham: the universe in one place
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Carrying on from the blinding light, the vision now opens up, showing the whole world inside a single form.

body.text: There Arjuna saw the entire universe gathered in one place, divided in countless ways within the body of the Lord of the gods. The word ekastham means gathered in one place. In the body of the god of gods, Arjuna sees the entire universe, all of it, held together in a single spot. Overwhelmed by this, Arjuna bows his head to the divine and speaks with folded hands.

verses.sa: ततः स विस्मयाविष्टो हृष्टरोमा धनञ्जयः । प्रणम्य शिरसा देवं कृताञ्जलिरभाषत ॥
verses.tr: Then, overwhelmed with wonder, Arjuna’s hair stood on end. He bowed his head to the divine and spoke with folded hands.
verses.angle: The body reacts before the mind
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna has just seen the divine form. Now his body reacts before his mind finds words. Listen to what his body does.

body.text: Then, overwhelmed with wonder, Arjuna’s hair stood on end. He bowed his head to the divine and spoke with folded hands. The verse says Arjuna was vismaya-avishtah, filled with wonder. His body reacts with hrishtha-roma, hair standing on end. He bows his head and speaks with folded hands. The body moves first, and only then does he find words. Arjuna now begins to speak, naming the gods he sees inside the Lord's cosmic form.
